# Research Report: Automated Pipeline for Static Image Object-by-Object Pop-up Video Animation with Synchronized Sound Effects

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Recommended Architecture

Building a pipeline that transforms a single static image into an animated reveal video (where objects pop up one by one with bounce effects and synchronized audio) is entirely achievable in Python. While there is no single out-of-the-box monolithic package that does all four steps under one command, this pipeline is constructed by combining **three proven open-source engineering pillars**:

```
[Static Image]
       │
       ▼
[1. Segmentation & Detection] ──► Extracts RGBA Cutouts + Binary Masks
       │                          (SAM 2, Grounded-SAM, or YOLO11-seg)
       ▼
[2. Background Plate Inpainting] ──► Removes objects & fills occluded background
       │                             (LaMa via simple-lama-inpainting)
       ▼
[3. Motion Graphics & Compositing] ◄── [4. Timed Sound Effects]
   (MoviePy / PIL or ManimCE)            (Pydub sub-millisecond audio mixer)
   - Eased Scaling (ease_out_back)       - Overlay SFX at exact pop timestamps
   - Centered Anchor Transformations
       │
       ▼
[Final MP4 Video with Audio]
```

---

## 2. Required Python Libraries

### A. Object Detection & Segmentation
*   **`segment-anything` / `segment-anything-2` (`sam2`)**: Meta AI's foundation models. Generates pixel-perfect alpha cutouts.
    *   *Prompt-free mode*: `SamAutomaticMaskGenerator` slices an entire image into all candidate object masks.
    *   *Repository*: [Meta SAM 2 GitHub](https://github.com/facebookresearch/segment-anything-2)
*   **`groundingdino-py` / `transformers` (Grounded-SAM)**: Combines Grounding DINO with SAM. Detects objects from arbitrary natural language text prompts (e.g., `"keyboard, coffee cup, glasses, book"`) and feeds bounding boxes into SAM for segmentation.
    *   *Repository*: [IDEA-Research/Grounded-Segment-Anything](https://github.com/IDEA-Research/Grounded-Segment-Anything)
*   **`ultralytics` (YOLOv8-seg / YOLO11-seg)**: High-speed alternative if processing latency matters and objects belong to standard classes (COCO 80 categories).
    *   *Repository*: [Ultralytics GitHub](https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics)
*   **`supervision` (Roboflow)**: Utility library for filtering masks, Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS), polygon extraction, and visualization.
    *   *Documentation*: [Roboflow Supervision](https://supervision.roboflow.com/)

### B. Background Inpainting & Alpha Image Processing
*   **`simple-lama-inpainting` (LaMa)**: Resolves the critical "occlusion problem." When objects are cut out and hidden on frame 0, this lightweight Python wrapper around LaMa (Large Mask Inpainting) reconstructs the empty background plate seamlessly.
    *   *PyPI*: [simple-lama-inpainting on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/simple-lama-inpainting/)
*   **`opencv-python` (`cv2`)**: Mask dilation (`cv2.dilate` to expand cutout boundaries to avoid edge fringing) and Gaussian feathering for smooth alpha transparency.
*   **`Pillow` (`PIL`)**: High-fidelity RGBA layer composition, bounding box cropping, and color space conversions.

### C. Animation & Video Compositing
*   **`moviepy` (v1.0.3 / v2.x)**: Handles timeline sequencing, dynamic scaling lambdas (`resize(lambda t: ...)`), layer positioning (`set_position`), and final MP4 encoding via FFmpeg.
    *   *Documentation*: [MoviePy Official Docs](https://zulko.github.io/moviepy/)
*   **`numpy`**: Evaluates custom spring/bounce easing functions (`ease_out_back` or `ease_out_bounce`).
*   **Alternative Python Engine — `manim` (Manim Community Edition)**: A programmatic animation engine with native `ImageMobject`, built-in `rate_func=ease_out_bounce` / `rate_func=ease_out_back`, and `self.add_sound()`.
    *   *Documentation*: [Manim Community Documentation](https://docs.manim.community/)

### D. Audio Synchronization
*   **`pydub`**: The gold standard in Python for sample-accurate audio mixing. Rather than relying solely on MoviePy's internal audio composition (which can suffer from timeline drift or click/pop artifacts), Pydub constructs a clean master audio track by placing sound effects at millisecond precision (`base.overlay(sfx, position=int(t * 1000))`).
    *   *Repository*: [Pydub GitHub](https://github.com/jiaaro/pydub)
*   **`ffmpeg`**: System backend required by both MoviePy and Pydub for muxing audio and video streams.

---

## 3. Proven Workflows, Repositories, and Reference Implementations

While no single monolithic tutorial exists for this exact combination, several prominent open-source projects validate each segment of the pipeline:

### 1. Layer Decomposition & Multi-Layer Extraction
*   **LayerCake ([github.com/VjiaoBlack/layercake](https://github.com/VjiaoBlack/layercake))**:
    *   Uses **SAM 2** and **SAM 3** to automatically slice photographs into depth-ordered transparent PNG layers with a clean background plate (`bg.png`). Demonstrates how to preserve full source dimensions across all RGBA layers for pixel-accurate compositing.
*   **Inpaint Anything ([github.com/geekyutao/Inpaint-Anything](https://github.com/geekyutao/Inpaint-Anything)) / arXiv:2304.06790 ([arxiv.org/abs/2304.06790](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06790))**:
    *   The benchmark workflow combining SAM masks with LaMa inpainting to remove objects from scenes and cleanly fill occluded spaces.
*   **Parallax-Maker ([github.com/provos/parallax-maker](https://github.com/provos/parallax-maker))**:
    *   Decomposes static images into 2.5D layers using SAM segmentation, monocular depth estimation, and inpainting.

### 2. Easing & Pop-up Video Animation Tutorials
*   **MoviePy Dynamic Scaling Animation ([Stack Overflow: Moviepy resize animation over time](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/43477218/moviepy-resize-animation-how-to-scale-image-over-time))**:
    *   Explains how to use MoviePy's `.resize(lambda t: ...)` method to interpolate scale factors dynamically over time.
*   **MoviePy Audio Synchronization ([Stack Overflow: CompositeAudioClip set_start](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62256985/moviepy-set-audio-at-specific-time))**:
    *   Shows how to time sound effects to specific seconds using `sound.set_start(timestamp)` inside `CompositeAudioClip`.
*   **Manim Easing & Audio ([Manim Docs: Rate Functions](https://docs.manim.community/en/stable/reference/manim.utils.rate_functions.html) & [Manim Docs: add_sound](https://docs.manim.community/en/stable/reference/manim.scene.scene.Scene.html#manim.scene.scene.Scene.add_sound))**:
    *   Shows Manim's native support for `rate_func=ease_out_bounce`, `rate_func=ease_out_back`, and `self.add_sound(sound_file)`.
*   **Remotion Spring Pop-up ([remotion.dev/docs/spring](https://www.remotion.dev/docs/spring))**:
    *   The React/TypeScript equivalent showing physics-based pop-up springs (`stiffness`, `damping`, `mass`). Useful if building a Node.js-based rendering microservice instead of pure Python.

---

## 4. Key Technical Challenges and Solutions

### Challenge 1: The Occlusion Hole Problem (What's Behind the Object?)
*   **The Issue**: If you start with a complete photograph, hiding Object A at $T=0$ leaves a gaping hole or black silhouette where Object A used to be.
*   **The Solution**: Reconstruct a **Clean Background Plate** before animating.
    1. Take the union of all detected object masks.
    2. Dilate the mask by 5–15 pixels using `cv2.dilate` to fully engulf edge pixels and shadows.
    3. Pass the dilated mask and original image to **LaMa** via `simple-lama-inpainting`.
    4. Use this inpainted image as the base video layer ($Z=0$), guaranteeing that before any object pops in, a clean background is shown.

### Challenge 2: Centered Anchor Resizing (Avoiding Coordinate Drift)
*   **The Issue**: In MoviePy, calling `.resize(lambda t: scale(t))` on an image scales it from the top-left origin $(0, 0)$ by default. If an object is located at $(X=800, Y=300)$, scaling it from $0 \to 1$ causes it to fly across the screen towards its destination rather than popping out from its own center.
*   **The Solution**: Crop each segmented object tightly to its bounding box $[x_{\min}, y_{\min}, x_{\max}, y_{\max}]$. Calculate its centroid $(c_x, c_y) = (x_{\min} + w/2, y_{\min} + h/2)$. In MoviePy, anchor the position dynamically:
    ```python
    clip = clip.resize(lambda t: scale_func(t)).set_position(
        lambda t: (cx - (clip.w * scale_func(t)) / 2, cy - (clip.h * scale_func(t)) / 2)
    )
    ```

### Challenge 3: Unnatural Linear Motion vs. Organic Easing
*   **The Issue**: A linear scale ($0.0 \to 1.0$) looks stiff and mechanical.
*   **The Solution**: Implement an **Overshoot Back-Out (`ease_out_back`)** or **Ease-Out Bounce** curve. In CSS/animation physics, `ease_out_back` scales the object slightly past $100\%$ (e.g., $115\%$), then snaps back to $100\%$, creating the classic cartoon "pop":
    $$f(p) = 1 + (s + 1)(p - 1)^3 + s(p - 1)^2 \quad \text{where } s \approx 1.70158$$

### Challenge 4: Edge Halos and Jagged Cutouts
*   **The Issue**: Binary masks from SAM/YOLO produce sharp, aliased, or haloed edges against the new background.
*   **The Solution**: Apply alpha feathering. Blur the binary alpha channel with a small Gaussian kernel ($3 \times 3$ or $5 \times 5$, $\sigma = 1.0$), then re-insert it as the 4th channel of the RGBA cutout.

### Challenge 5: Audio-Visual Desync & MoviePy Audio Clicks
*   **The Issue**: MoviePy's `CompositeAudioClip` can occasionally cause micro-stutters or audio crackling when layering many short WAV files.
*   **The Solution**: Decouple audio synthesis. Use `pydub` to generate a master `.wav` file on an exact millisecond timeline, then attach it to the final `CompositeVideoClip` using `.set_audio(AudioFileClip("master_audio.wav"))`.

---

## 5. Production-Ready Python Implementation Blueprint

Here is an end-to-end, runnable implementation illustrating the complete architecture:

```python
"""
End-to-End Pipeline: Static Image -> Segment -> Inpaint BG -> Pop-up Animation -> Video with SFX
Dependencies:
    pip install moviepy pydub simple-lama-inpainting opencv-python pillow numpy segment-anything
"""

import os
import cv2
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from pydub import AudioSegment
from pydub.generators import Sine
from moviepy.editor import ImageClip, CompositeVideoClip, AudioFileClip

# =====================================================================
# 1. MATHEMATICAL EASING FUNCTION (Overshoot Pop-up)
# =====================================================================
def ease_out_back(p: float, s: float = 1.70158) -> float:
    """Overshoots slightly beyond 1.0 before settling at 1.0."""
    p = max(0.0, min(1.0, p))
    p -= 1.0
    return p * p * ((s + 1) * p + s) + 1.0

def make_scale_fn(pop_duration: float):
    def scale_fn(t: float) -> float:
        if t <= 0:
            return 0.001  # MoviePy fails on absolute 0 width/height
        if t >= pop_duration:
            return 1.0
        return max(0.001, ease_out_back(t / pop_duration))
    return scale_fn

# =====================================================================
# 2. SYNTHETIC SOUND EFFECT GENERATOR (Fallback if no WAV file provided)
# =====================================================================
def generate_pop_sfx(output_path="pop.wav"):
    """Generates a pleasant 80ms pitch-dropping 'pop' sound."""
    sample = Sine(800).to_audio_segment(duration=40).fade_out(30) + \
             Sine(400).to_audio_segment(duration=40).fade_out(30)
    sample.export(output_path, format="wav")
    return output_path

# =====================================================================
# 3. SEGMENTATION & INPAINTING (Mock / Standard API Interface)
# =====================================================================
def run_segmentation_and_inpainting(image_path: str):
    """
    In production, replace with:
        from segment_anything import sam_model_registry, SamAutomaticMaskGenerator
        from simple_lama_inpainting import SimpleLama
    Returns:
        background_img (PIL.Image RGB),
        cutouts (list of dicts containing 'rgba', 'bbox', 'centroid')
    """
    orig_img = Image.open(image_path).convert("RGB")
    w, h = orig_img.size

    # Example: 2 mock segmented objects (e.g. left item, right item)
    # With SAM, each item is extracted using: item_rgba = orig * mask
    cutouts = []
    
    # Mock Object 1 (Left circle/box)
    rgba1 = Image.new("RGBA", (200, 200), (255, 80, 80, 255))
    cutouts.append({
        "image": rgba1,
        "bbox": (150, h // 2 - 100, 350, h // 2 + 100),
        "centroid": (250, h // 2)
    })
    
    # Mock Object 2 (Right circle/box)
    rgba2 = Image.new("RGBA", (220, 220), (80, 180, 255, 255))
    cutouts.append({
        "image": rgba2,
        "bbox": (w - 370, h // 2 - 110, w - 150, h // 2 + 110),
        "centroid": (w - 260, h // 2)
    })

    # In production:
    # simple_lama = SimpleLama()
    # background_img = simple_lama(orig_img, combined_dilated_mask)
    background_img = Image.new("RGB", (w, h), (240, 242, 245))

    return orig_img, background_img, cutouts

# =====================================================================
# 4. TIMELINE COMPOSITING & ANIMATION ENGINE
# =====================================================================
def build_animated_video(
    image_path: str,
    output_video_path: str = "animated_popup.mp4",
    pop_duration: float = 0.45,
    interval_between_pops: float = 0.8,
    trailing_pause: float = 1.5,
    fps: int = 30
):
    orig_img, bg_img, cutouts = run_segmentation_and_inpainting(image_path)
    w, h = orig_img.size
    num_objects = len(cutouts)

    # Compute timeline timestamps
    total_duration = (num_objects * interval_between_pops) + trailing_pause
    pop_fn = make_scale_fn(pop_duration)

    # Base Background Clip
    bg_np = np.array(bg_img)
    bg_clip = ImageClip(bg_np).set_duration(total_duration)

    video_clips = [bg_clip]
    pop_sfx_path = generate_pop_sfx("pop_effect.wav")
    sfx_segment = AudioSegment.from_file(pop_sfx_path)
    
    # Master Audio track (silent baseline)
    master_audio = AudioSegment.silent(duration=int(total_duration * 1000))

    # Animate each object popping up sequentially
    for idx, obj in enumerate(cutouts):
        start_time = idx * interval_between_pops
        clip_duration = total_duration - start_time
        cx, cy = obj["centroid"]
        
        # Convert RGBA to NumPy
        rgba_np = np.array(obj["image"])
        obj_clip = ImageClip(rgba_np, ismask=False, transparent=True)
        obj_w, obj_h = obj["image"].size

        # Apply eased scaling & centered anchoring
        animated_clip = (
            obj_clip
            .set_start(start_time)
            .set_duration(clip_duration)
            .resize(lambda t: pop_fn(t))
            .set_position(lambda t: (
                cx - (obj_w * pop_fn(t)) / 2.0,
                cy - (obj_h * pop_fn(t)) / 2.0
            ))
        )
        video_clips.append(animated_clip)

        # Overlay Sound Effect at exact pop timestamp
        master_audio = master_audio.overlay(
            sfx_segment,
            position=int(start_time * 1000)
        )

    # Export master audio
    temp_audio_path = "master_soundtrack.wav"
    master_audio.export(temp_audio_path, format="wav")

    # Final Video Assembly
    final_video = CompositeVideoClip(video_clips, size=(w, h)).set_duration(total_duration)
    final_video = final_video.set_audio(AudioFileClip(temp_audio_path))

    final_video.write_videofile(
        output_video_path,
        fps=fps,
        codec="libx264",
        audio_codec="aac"
    )

    # Cleanup temporary audio
    if os.path.exists(temp_audio_path):
        os.remove(temp_audio_path)
    print(f"Exported successfully to {output_video_path}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Create test canvas
    dummy_input = "test_scene.png"
    Image.new("RGB", (1280, 720), (255, 255, 255)).save(dummy_input)
    build_animated_video(dummy_input)
```

---

## 6. Comparison: MoviePy vs. Manim vs. Remotion

| Feature / Metric | **MoviePy + PIL + Pydub** (Recommended) | **Manim (ManimCE)** | **Remotion** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Language** | Pure Python | Pure Python | TypeScript / React |
| **Animation Paradigm** | Time-parameterized functions (`t -> f(t)`) | Mathematical Scene objects (`Scene.play`) | Frame-based component rendering |
| **Popup / Easing** | Custom math formula (`ease_out_back`) | Built-in (`rate_func=ease_out_bounce`) | Built-in physics (`spring()`) |
| **Sound Handling** | Sub-millisecond via `pydub` | Built-in `self.add_sound()` | Native `<Audio>` components |
| **Pixel Control** | Direct NumPy/OpenCV RGBA arrays | Geometry & Vector first; Mobject wrapper | CSS styles & HTML5 canvas |
| **Backend Integration** | Lightweight, headless, minimal dependencies | Requires LaTeX/Cairo dependencies | Requires Node.js and headless Chrome |

---

## 7. Citations & Reference URLs

1. **Meta AI Segment Anything (SAM)**: [https://github.com/facebookresearch/segment-anything](https://github.com/facebookresearch/segment-anything)
2. **Meta AI Segment Anything 2 (SAM 2)**: [https://github.com/facebookresearch/segment-anything-2](https://github.com/facebookresearch/segment-anything-2)
3. **Inpaint Anything (SAM + LaMa)**: [https://github.com/geekyutao/Inpaint-Anything](https://github.com/geekyutao/Inpaint-Anything) & [https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06790](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06790)
4. **LayerCake (SAM 2 depth-ordered PNG layer decomposition)**: [https://github.com/VjiaoBlack/layercake](https://github.com/VjiaoBlack/layercake)
5. **Grounded-Segment-Anything (Grounding DINO + SAM)**: [https://github.com/IDEA-Research/Grounded-Segment-Anything](https://github.com/IDEA-Research/Grounded-Segment-Anything)
6. **Simple LaMa Inpainting (PyPI)**: [https://pypi.org/project/simple-lama-inpainting/](https://pypi.org/project/simple-lama-inpainting/)
7. **MoviePy Documentation & ImageClip**: [https://zulko.github.io/moviepy/](https://zulko.github.io/moviepy/)
8. **MoviePy Dynamic Resize Animation Discussion**: [https://stackoverflow.com/questions/43477218/moviepy-resize-animation-how-to-scale-image-over-time](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/43477218/moviepy-resize-animation-how-to-scale-image-over-time)
9. **MoviePy Audio Synchronization (`set_start`)**: [https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62256985/moviepy-set-audio-at-specific-time](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62256985/moviepy-set-audio-at-specific-time)
10. **Manim Community Easing Functions**: [https://docs.manim.community/en/stable/reference/manim.utils.rate_functions.html](https://docs.manim.community/en/stable/reference/manim.utils.rate_functions.html)
11. **Manim Sound Support (`add_sound`)**: [https://docs.manim.community/en/stable/reference/manim.scene.scene.Scene.html#manim.scene.scene.Scene.add_sound](https://docs.manim.community/en/stable/reference/manim.scene.scene.Scene.html#manim.scene.scene.Scene.add_sound)
12. **Remotion Spring Animation**: [https://www.remotion.dev/docs/spring](https://www.remotion.dev/docs/spring)
13. **Pydub Audio Library**: [https://github.com/jiaaro/pydub](https://github.com/jiaaro/pydub)

## 4. Key Technical Challenges and Solutions

### Challenge 1: The Occlusion Hole Problem (What's Behind the Object?)
*   **The Issue**: If you start with a complete photograph, hiding Object A at $T=0$ leaves a gaping hole or black silhouette where Object A used to be.
*   **The Solution**: Reconstruct a **Clean Background Plate** before animating.
    1. Take the union of all detected object masks.
    2. Dilate the mask by 5–15 pixels using `cv2.dilate` to fully engulf edge pixels and shadows.
    3. Pass the dilated mask and original image to **LaMa** via `simple-lama-inpainting`.
    4. Use this inpainted image as the base video layer ($Z=0$), guaranteeing that before any object pops in, a clean background is shown.

### Challenge 2: Centered Anchor Resizing (Avoiding Coordinate Drift)
*   **The Issue**: In MoviePy, calling `.resize(lambda t: scale(t))` on an image scales it from the top-left origin $(0, 0)$ by default. If an object is located at $(X=800, Y=300)$, scaling it from $0 \to 1$ causes it to fly across the screen towards its destination rather than popping out from its own center.
*   **The Solution**: Crop each segmented object tightly to its bounding box $[x_{\min}, y_{\min}, x_{\max}, y_{\max}]$. Calculate its centroid $(c_x, c_y) = (x_{\min} + w/2, y_{\min} + h/2)$. In MoviePy, anchor the position dynamically:
    ```python
    clip = clip.resize(lambda t: scale_func(t)).set_position(
        lambda t: (cx - (clip.w * scale_func(t)) / 2, cy - (clip.h * scale_func(t)) / 2)
    )
    ```

### Challenge 3: Unnatural Linear Motion vs. Organic Easing
*   **The Issue**: A linear scale ($0.0 \to 1.0$) looks stiff and mechanical.
*   **The Solution**: Implement an **Overshoot Back-Out (`ease_out_back`)** or **Ease-Out Bounce** curve. In CSS/animation physics, `ease_out_back` scales the object slightly past $100\%$ (e.g., $115\%$), then snaps back to $100\%$, creating the classic cartoon "pop":
    $$f(p) = 1 + (s + 1)(p - 1)^3 + s(p - 1)^2 \quad \text{where } s \approx 1.70158$$

### Challenge 4: Edge Halos and Jagged Cutouts
*   **The Issue**: Binary masks from SAM/YOLO produce sharp, aliased, or haloed edges against the new background.
*   **The Solution**: Apply alpha feathering. Blur the binary alpha channel with a small Gaussian kernel ($3 \times 3$ or $5 \times 5$, $\sigma = 1.0$), then re-insert it as the 4th channel of the RGBA cutout.

### Challenge 5: Audio-Visual Desync & MoviePy Audio Clicks
*   **The Issue**: MoviePy's `CompositeAudioClip` can occasionally cause micro-stutters or audio crackling when layering many short WAV files.
*   **The Solution**: Decouple audio synthesis. Use `pydub` to generate a master `.wav` file on an exact millisecond timeline, then attach it to the final `CompositeVideoClip` using `.set_audio(AudioFileClip("master_audio.wav"))`.

## 5. Production-Ready Python Implementation Blueprint

Here is an end-to-end, runnable implementation illustrating the complete architecture:

```python
"""
End-to-End Pipeline: Static Image -> Segment -> Inpaint BG -> Pop-up Animation -> Video with SFX
Dependencies:
    pip install moviepy pydub simple-lama-inpainting opencv-python pillow numpy segment-anything
"""

import os
import cv2
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from pydub import AudioSegment
from pydub.generators import Sine
from moviepy.editor import ImageClip, CompositeVideoClip, AudioFileClip

# =====================================================================
# 1. MATHEMATICAL EASING FUNCTION (Overshoot Pop-up)
# =====================================================================
def ease_out_back(p: float, s: float = 1.70158) -> float:
    """Overshoots slightly beyond 1.0 before settling at 1.0."""
    p = max(0.0, min(1.0, p))
    p -= 1.0
    return p * p * ((s + 1) * p + s) + 1.0

def make_scale_fn(pop_duration: float):
    def scale_fn(t: float) -> float:
        if t <= 0:
            return 0.001  # MoviePy fails on absolute 0 width/height
        if t >= pop_duration:
            return 1.0
        return max(0.001, ease_out_back(t / pop_duration))
    return scale_fn

# =====================================================================
# 2. SYNTHETIC SOUND EFFECT GENERATOR (Fallback if no WAV file provided)
# =====================================================================
def generate_pop_sfx(output_path="pop.wav"):
    """Generates a pleasant 80ms pitch-dropping 'pop' sound."""
    sample = Sine(800).to_audio_segment(duration=40).fade_out(30) + \
             Sine(400).to_audio_segment(duration=40).fade_out(30)
    sample.export(output_path, format="wav")
    return output_path

# =====================================================================
# 3. SEGMENTATION & INPAINTING (Mock / Standard API Interface)
# =====================================================================
def run_segmentation_and_inpainting(image_path: str):
    """
    In production, replace with:
        from segment_anything import sam_model_registry, SamAutomaticMaskGenerator
        from simple_lama_inpainting import SimpleLama
    Returns:
        background_img (PIL.Image RGB),
        cutouts (list of dicts containing 'rgba', 'bbox', 'centroid')
    """
    orig_img = Image.open(image_path).convert("RGB")
    w, h = orig_img.size

    # Example: 2 mock segmented objects (e.g. left item, right item)
    # With SAM, each item is extracted using: item_rgba = orig * mask
    cutouts = []
    
    # Mock Object 1 (Left circle/box)
    rgba1 = Image.new("RGBA", (200, 200), (255, 80, 80, 255))
    cutouts.append({
        "image": rgba1,
        "bbox": (150, h // 2 - 100, 350, h // 2 + 100),
        "centroid": (250, h // 2)
    })
    
    # Mock Object 2 (Right circle/box)
    rgba2 = Image.new("RGBA", (220, 220), (80, 180, 255, 255))
    cutouts.append({
        "image": rgba2,
        "bbox": (w - 370, h // 2 - 110, w - 150, h // 2 + 110),
        "centroid": (w - 260, h // 2)
    })

    # In production:
    # simple_lama = SimpleLama()
    # background_img = simple_lama(orig_img, combined_dilated_mask)
    background_img = Image.new("RGB", (w, h), (240, 242, 245))

    return orig_img, background_img, cutouts

# =====================================================================
# 4. TIMELINE COMPOSITING & ANIMATION ENGINE
# =====================================================================
def build_animated_video(
    image_path: str,
    output_video_path: str = "animated_popup.mp4",
    pop_duration: float = 0.45,
    interval_between_pops: float = 0.8,
    trailing_pause: float = 1.5,
    fps: int = 30
):
    orig_img, bg_img, cutouts = run_segmentation_and_inpainting(image_path)
    w, h = orig_img.size
    num_objects = len(cutouts)

    # Compute timeline timestamps
    total_duration = (num_objects * interval_between_pops) + trailing_pause
    pop_fn = make_scale_fn(pop_duration)

    # Base Background Clip
    bg_np = np.array(bg_img)
    bg_clip = ImageClip(bg_np).set_duration(total_duration)

    video_clips = [bg_clip]
    pop_sfx_path = generate_pop_sfx("pop_effect.wav")
    sfx_segment = AudioSegment.from_file(pop_sfx_path)
    
    # Master Audio track (silent baseline)
    master_audio = AudioSegment.silent(duration=int(total_duration * 1000))

    # Animate each object popping up sequentially
    for idx, obj in enumerate(cutouts):
        start_time = idx * interval_between_pops
        clip_duration = total_duration - start_time
        cx, cy = obj["centroid"]
        
        # Convert RGBA to NumPy
        rgba_np = np.array(obj["image"])
        obj_clip = ImageClip(rgba_np, ismask=False, transparent=True)
        obj_w, obj_h = obj["image"].size

        # Apply eased scaling & centered anchoring
        animated_clip = (
            obj_clip
            .set_start(start_time)
            .set_duration(clip_duration)
            .resize(lambda t: pop_fn(t))
            .set_position(lambda t: (
                cx - (obj_w * pop_fn(t)) / 2.0,
                cy - (obj_h * pop_fn(t)) / 2.0
            ))
        )
        video_clips.append(animated_clip)

        # Overlay Sound Effect at exact pop timestamp
        master_audio = master_audio.overlay(
            sfx_segment,
            position=int(start_time * 1000)
        )

    # Export master audio
    temp_audio_path = "master_soundtrack.wav"
    master_audio.export(temp_audio_path, format="wav")

    # Final Video Assembly
    final_video = CompositeVideoClip(video_clips, size=(w, h)).set_duration(total_duration)
    final_video = final_video.set_audio(AudioFileClip(temp_audio_path))

    final_video.write_videofile(
        output_video_path,
        fps=fps,
        codec="libx264",
        audio_codec="aac"
    )

    # Cleanup temporary audio
    if os.path.exists(temp_audio_path):
        os.remove(temp_audio_path)
    print(f"Exported successfully to {output_video_path}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Create test canvas
    dummy_input = "test_scene.png"
    Image.new("RGB", (1280, 720), (255, 255, 255)).save(dummy_input)
    build_animated_video(dummy_input)
```

## 6. Comparison: MoviePy vs. Manim vs. Remotion

| Feature / Metric | **MoviePy + PIL + Pydub** (Recommended) | **Manim (ManimCE)** | **Remotion** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Language** | Pure Python | Pure Python | TypeScript / React |
| **Animation Paradigm** | Time-parameterized functions (`t -> f(t)`) | Mathematical Scene objects (`Scene.play`) | Frame-based component rendering |
| **Popup / Easing** | Custom math formula (`ease_out_back`) | Built-in (`rate_func=ease_out_bounce`) | Built-in physics (`spring()`) |
| **Sound Handling** | Sub-millisecond via `pydub` | Built-in `self.add_sound()` | Native `<Audio>` components |
| **Pixel Control** | Direct NumPy/OpenCV RGBA arrays | Geometry & Vector first; Mobject wrapper | CSS styles & HTML5 canvas |
| **Backend Integration** | Lightweight, headless, minimal dependencies | Requires LaTeX/Cairo dependencies | Requires Node.js and headless Chrome |
